blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it

findings.recommendation: The seat-adding branch sits six levels deep (for row / if email / match / if plan / for seat / if not present / if '@'), so a newcomer has to hold every enclosing condition in mind to know when a seat is added. Three business rules are expressed with no word of why: rows with an empty email are silently skipped (line 15), seats are only added to an existing account when its plan differs from the row's (line 18) — a reader cannot tell whether this is intended or an inverted test without the plan — and seats without an '@' are dropped (lines 21 and 32). The seat loop with the '@' filter is also duplicated between the `Some` and `None` arms. Flatten without changing behavior: `continue` early on an empty email, extract a helper such as `add_new_seats(db, account_id, seats, existing) -> Result<usize, DbError>` with a named predicate (e.g. `is_seat_email`) used by both arms, and add a one-line comment giving the reason for the plan-change condition and the skipped rows.
findings.title: `import` nests six levels deep and hides its rules in unexplained conditions
